To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the structure of the macromolecule can be determined directly from the diffraction data, without the need for an initial model, and that (ii) this is possible because the macromolecular crystals are composed of a large number of copies of the same macromolecule, which is a prerequisite for a successful experimental phasing.

the SAD method can be used to solve the phase problem in macromolecular crystallography, and that it is possible to solve the phase and model-building problems in macromolecular X-ray crystallography in a fully automatic way, without the need of human intervention.

(a) the SAD method is the most efficient and robust method for phasing macromolecular structures, (b) the SAD phasing method can be used with crystals that diffract to 2.5 Å or better and (c) the SIRAS method is an alternative to SAD that is applicable for structures that diffract poorly.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the molecular structure of organic compounds and the elucidation of molecular structures in the solid state.
the development of new methods of macromolecular crystallography, and their implementation in the programs mentioned above.
the development, implementation and use of methods and programs that can be used for the determination of protein and other macromolecular structures from X-ray diffraction data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

experimental phasing of protein crystals has become routine, and that it is the method of choice for solving the structure of proteins and other macromolecules that are not isomorphous with any known protein.
experimental phasing is an extremely powerful and reliable method of solving the structures of biological macromolecules.
SHELX is the most powerful and versatile program package available for the experimental phasing of protein and nucleic-acid crystal structures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SHELX has been used in 1,000 structures solved by molecular replacement and in about 100 structures solved by direct methods.
the programs have now been used to solve more than 200 structures.
the SHELX suite of programs is a very useful tool for the solution of macromolecular structures by experimental phasing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the phasing of protein structures can be automated, provided that a high-quality data set has been collected, and that the structure can be solved by the molecular-replacement method.

, in many cases, the experimental phasing of a macromolecule can be performed by a novice user with the help of the program SHELXE, without the need for any prior experience with the program or with macromolecular crystallography.

the phasing of macromo­lecules can be achieved by the use of experimental data in combination with a small number of heavy-atom derivatives, provided that the heavy-atom positions are accurately known.
